correctness.rationale: Exact zero atom and adjacent-side integral are algebraically derived with all labeling factors; the O(t) remainder is proved using supporting-line separation and nonzero partial derivatives at every possible zero in a three-distinct-side allocation. The universal coefficient bound and rectangle equality are exact. The marked law follows from the normalized du/u Jacobian and conditional uniformity. Standalone direct numerical checks passed but are not used as proof.

originality.rationale: A prior complete exact perimeter-sampled three-point area distribution covers the triangular-host case; the present claim is restricted to fixed convex polygons with at least four genuine sides. The m=3 result does not imply the general m>=4 coefficient, sharp rectangle extremality or multiedge marked conditional law. Other inspected works cover interior sampling, chord lengths, N->infinity boundary hull deficits, smooth curved boundaries or positive square thresholds. Historical novelty for >=4 is provisional.
residual_risks: An unindexed classical polygonal boundary-triangle area distribution could imply the coefficient; negative searches alone do not prove priority.

value.rationale: The complete convex-polygon hosts with at least four sides leading small-area law resolves the basic degeneracy asymptotics of random perimeter triangles, including its nontrivial atom, universal sharp shape lower bound and equality class, and conditional logarithmic mechanism. The result contrasts with smooth boundary scaling and distinguishes shapes through their corner weights. It is a natural many-sided geometric-probability invariant rather than a bespoke computational slice.
